newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods gain as NYMEX offsets weaker diffs.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods gain as NYMEX offsets weaker diffs.

text.p: U.S. spot oil products prices ended higher late Wednesday as NYMEX futures offset mostly lower differentials, traders said, with most of the focus on weakening Gulf Coast gasoline.

The dip in gasoline diffs pared the modest gains seen Tuesday, according to traders, made on the outage of the 102,000 barrel per day (bpd) catalytic cracking unit at Exxon's Baton Rouge, Louisiana refinery.

But the bullish impact proved short lived because of statements the outage would last only a few days, traders said. By late Wednesday, offers on Gulf back 36th cycle conventional unleaded gasoline had slipped one cent to 5.75 cents below the January print.
"The Exxon rally fizzled and we came back down to where we were a week and a half ago," one Gulf trader said, adding, "there was good buying" at the new lower prices.
But January NYMEX gasoline stemmed the pain, settling 1.40 cents higher at 71.17 cents a gallon after hitting a contract high of 71.50 intraday.
It was helped by EIA data released Wednesday showing a 3.3 million barrel draw on stocks for the week ending Dec 13, versus Tuesday's API estimate of a 3.1 million barrel draw.
